identity.title: $PhyWorldBench$: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Physical Realism in Text-to-Video Models

problem.claim: Evaluate whether text-to-video models simulate physical phenomena and follow physics-consistent or intentionally anti-physics prompts.

gap.claim: Models’ ability to accurately simulate physical phenomena remains unresolved despite progress in photorealistic generation.

contributions.claim: PhyWorldBench evaluates physical realism across fundamental, composite, human/animal-motion, and anti-physics scenarios.
The paper introduces a zero-shot method using current MLLMs to assess physics realism, alongside large-scale human evaluation.
The paper evaluates ten text-to-video models, evenly split between open-source and proprietary systems, on curated physical-phenomena prompts.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their benchmark by including an Anti-Physics category that tests intentional physics violations while requiring logical consistency.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating 10 state-of-the-art models—five open-source and five proprietary—with detailed comparison and analysis.
The authors report systematic testing across 1,050 curated prompts covering fundamental, composite, and anti-physics scenarios, identifying pivotal physics-adherence challenges.
The authors report deriving targeted prompt-crafting recommendations after examining performance across physical phenomena and prompt types.

narrative_sequence.summary: Photorealistic video generation has advanced, but accurate physical simulation remains unresolved.
PhyWorldBench evaluates physics adherence across multiple phenomenon levels and adds intentional anti-physics instructions.
The study combines large-scale human evaluation with a proposed zero-shot MLLM-based physics-realism assessment.
Ten models are tested on 1,050 curated prompts to identify physics-related challenges and formulate prompt recommendations.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark separates fundamental, composite, and anti-physics scenarios and varies prompt types when analyzing model performance.

lessons.interpretation: Explicitly partitioning task regimes can reveal whether failures concern physical knowledge, compositional interaction, or instruction following.
lessons.application: Design evaluations with separate regime labels and report results by regime rather than relying only on an aggregate score.
lessons.exception: This partitioning may be unsuitable when the application has too few examples per regime for meaningful comparison.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide model-level scores, metric definitions, statistical uncertainty, or concrete failure examples.
The zero-shot MLLM method and its agreement with human evaluation are not described.
The targeted prompt recommendations are not specified.
